_comment: THE EXPECTATION-SOURCE REGISTRY. Every check in this kit declares two
things: the SUBJECT it asserts about, and the ARTIFACT its EXPECTATION is
read from. `tools/expectation_lint.py` fails when those are the same
artifact and no waiver explains why.
This file exists because the same defect was found eight times by six
independent adoption walks, each time wearing a different hat, and the
operating architecture's own promotion rule says a prose rule that keeps
failing gets promoted to a mechanical layer. The design question 'where
does this check's expectation come from?' is now an answer every check
expectation_from: "inline" means hand-written literals in the checking
code. Those are the specification, they do not move when the code moves,
and they are deliberately out of scope.
ADDING A CHECK? Add a row. The lint cross-checks the fixture family
against hook_fixtures.py, so an unregistered fixture is caught; for
everything else, an absent row is invisible - the residual, named in

checks.subject: kit.config:FORBIDDEN_SPAWN_TIER
checks.reason: THE ORIGINAL INSTANCE. The payload names the tier the rule forbids, and both come from kit.config, so fixture and rule move in lockstep - weaken the key and the fixture weakens with it, still green. Unavoidable for a config-driven rule: the fixture's job is 'the hook honours whatever the config says'. Covered STRUCTURALLY instead: kit.config is in JUDGE_PATHS, so any uncommitted change to it reds the `judges` gate; and the fixture additionally asserts the deny REASON renders the configured tier, which a placeholder value cannot satisfy.

checks.subject: kit.config:MODEL_EXEMPT_TYPES
checks.reason: Same shape as fixture:j, same structural cover (kit.config in JUDGE_PATHS). Weaker in practice than j was: fixture c's payload is hard-coded, so widening the exempt list moves the hook's answer out from under an independent expectation and IS caught.

checks.subject: kit.config:PROTECTED_PATH
checks.reason: The payload is built from the configured path when one is set. Narrowed twice since: when the path is UNSET the payload uses a synthetic probe no config can name (so an unconfigured tripwire can no longer pass by matching its own placeholder), and the accept-set is now exactly `ask` when no cert-green token exists rather than {ask, allow}. Structural cover: kit.config in JUDGE_PATHS.

checks.subject: kit.config:PROTECTED_PATH
checks.reason: As fixture:l, for the Edit branch.

checks.subject: .claude/settings.json
checks.reason: INSTANCE 6, and only half-closable. Whether the hook is wired can only be read from the settings file itself; there is no second source for the harness's intent. What WAS closable is startability - the script a matched command names is now checked against the FILESYSTEM, an independent artifact, and a missing one reports UNSTARTABLE. Residual, accepted: a settings file that is internally consistent and wrong (wired to the correct path of the wrong hook) reads as armed.

checks.subject: QUICKSTART.md
checks.reason: Not self-referential by artifact - the checkpoints are hand-transcribed from the document into the walker, so an edit to one does not move the other. That is also its weakness, and a different one: the walker can drift out of date with the prose it transcribes. It runs the COMMANDS, not the explanations. Named in KNOWN-ISSUES as a residual.

checks.subject: modules/03-verification/verify.py:git_excluded
checks.reason: The control for the SHIPPED exclusion probe, where check:judged-paths-not-excluded covers only how the startup assertion reacts to an injected answer. The phase plants a real ignore rule over a real judge path in a real repository, in both rule shapes, and compares the runner against `git check-ignore` run independently. It exists because the first version of the probe corrupted every path it asked about and all three gates stayed green: an injected-answer check cannot see a transport defect.

checks.subject: tools/kit_render.py:rendering
checks.reason: Not self-referential by artifact, and deliberately so. document_order() renders the same templates BY HAND - a person's transcription of QUICKSTART - and phase 13 requires the tool's rendering to match it byte for byte (CLAUDE.md, the collaboration profile, TOKEN-LEDGER.md) and key for key (the structural settings merge). The two authorities are kept apart on purpose: the walk must never call the tool and the tool must never read the walk, or the kit loses its only independent expectation of what a rendered file looks like. When they disagree the arbiter is neither of them - it is the QUICKSTART step the hand model transcribes, and on this phase's first run the document ruled for the tool. Scope: this row covers the RENDERING sub-steps only; the guard assertions in the same phase are registered separately at smoke:phase13-render-guards. Residuals: the walk can drift out of date with the prose it transcribes; and the walk copies three of the four ledgers unrendered at Step 7, so JUDGMENT-LEDGER, FAILURE-FLOOR and LESSONS are checked against Step 7's printed checkpoint rather than diffed - every slot they carry is already covered by the CLAUDE.md byte-diff, and TOKEN-LEDGER is hand-rendered because RATIO_CEILING appears nowhere else.

checks.subject: tools/kit_render.py:containment
checks.reason: The same phase also asserts the two containment guards END TO END - a real subprocess, a real target repository, a real kit checkout - and those expectations do not come from the hand model. Guard 1 is measured by pointing a run at the kit clone and checking the kit tree afterwards; guard 1b by a LEDGERS_DIR that climbs out of the target and checking that the outside directory was never created; guard 2 by hashing every hand-rendered file before and after. The tool's own selftest proves the same refusals in process, which cannot see a filesystem that disagrees with the decision layer - the same argument smoke:phase12 makes about the exclusion probe.

checks.subject: tools/kit_doctor.py:KIT_VERSION
checks.reason: Two artifacts on purpose. The stamp records which kit release a tree was adopted from; the constant records which release the tools came from. Neither can be checked against the FILES - a version stamp is a claim by whoever last copied - but the two disagreeing is exactly the state a partial re-copy leaves behind, and that is mechanically checkable.

checks.subject: kit.config
checks.reason: The rule for 'is this key configured or still an example value' is imported from the shipped hook rather than re-implemented in the doctor. A fourth reader of that rule is the arrangement that produced the original defect.

checks.subject: modules/03-verification/verify.py:GATES
checks.reason: Three disjuncts, two of them structural properties of the gate table judged against hand-written rules (a require pattern with no capture group; a floor of 1 or less), and the third read from the FILESYSTEM (no docs/ORACLE-<gate>.md page). Registered as inline because the two rules that decide vacuity are hand-written literals; the filesystem half is named here so the row is not read as covering less than it does.

checks.subject: .claude/cert-green.json
checks.reason: Whether a token still covers the tree is git's answer (the newest commit touching CERT_PATHS is contained in the token's sha, and those paths are clean). What the check ALSO does is print the honest label on every run - the token is unsigned and forgeable by anything that can write a file - and that half has no expectation source because it is not a measurement. It is a disclosure, and it is the control.

checks.subject: checks-registry.json
checks.reason: The registry can only be checked against itself for internal consistency - there is no independent source for what a check's expectation ought to be. What it therefore cannot catch is an entry that is simply ABSENT. Narrowed for TWO families now, whose ids are recovered from the source and cross-checked both ways: the hook fixtures in hook_fixtures.py, and the doctor's checks in tools/kit_doctor.py. The doctor was the reason to generalise the cross-check rather than trust the author - ten unregistered checks in one commit would have grown this blind spot faster than the lint that discloses it. Everything outside those two families still depends on the author adding a row. Stated as a residual in KNOWN-ISSUES rather than presented as closed.
